gate: K4 third precondition (docs/architecture.md §8 Stack Bytecode VM Status: "Re-evaluate the bytecode architecture only when ... PMU evidence shows operand traffic / dispatch as the main bottleneck"), preserved by qjs_alignment_charter_transition.md K4
why_this_is_not_a_spike: E1 profiles the shipping engine on the shipping suite. It builds no candidate binary, changes no code, and compares nothing. It therefore does not touch the 2026-08-27 ruling that deferred the register-vs-stack spike (decision 2); it produces the evidence K4 requires before that spike could even be justified.
spec_basis: docs/perf/opcode-design.md §9.5 (evidence ladder E1/E1.5/E2), §2.2 (58 ids and roughly a third of dynamic instructions are stack-machine bookkeeping; 34.1%/37.6% across two harnesses), §6.4 (the three-skeleton floor pinned cost-per-dispatch, not dispatch count)
docs/perf/measurement-contracts.md (all clauses; clause 8 insn+cycles same run)
question: What share of suite cycles is spent inside the handlers that a register machine would not execute at all?

scope.measured_set: TIER 1 (counts toward the verdict) -- 68 handlers a register machine would not execute at all: 48 slot moves (get/put/set x loc/arg/var_ref x {0,1,2,3,8,wide}; loc 18 + arg 15 + var_ref 15), 9 stack shuffles (dup/swap/nip/nip_catch/insert2/insert3/perm3/perm4/rot3l), drop, and 10 fusion opcodes whose PREFIX HALF is a pure slot move (get_loc0_field, get_loc2_field, get_loc2_field2, get_loc8_push_1, get_loc8_push_2, get_loc8_push_i8, get_var_ref0_get_loc8, put_loc8_get_loc8, push_this_put_loc0, put_loc0_get_loc0). The fusion ten are in Tier 1 because a fusion opcode is a PREFIX SUBSTITUTION (opcode-design.md 10.2b): it owns one byte, does the first half, and tail-calls the untouched following instruction. Its recorded executions therefore ARE executions of the first half, and for these ten the first half is a slot move. Together Tier 1 is 34.1% + 9.3% = ~43% of the zoo census.
scope.reference_set: all other handlers, reported alongside so the Tier 1 share is a share of something
scope.excluded: nothing is excluded a priori. The earlier draft excluded cold-shell handlers on the assumption that they share function bodies; that was checked on 2026-08-27 and is false -- each coldStd(body) instantiation is comptime-distinct. What is real is the 15 shared-entry groups in method.resolution_measured, none of which straddles the measured/reference boundary.
scope.third_bucket: TIER 2 (reported, does NOT count toward the verdict) -- constant materialisation: the four fusion opcodes whose prefix half pushes a constant (push_0_or 9.00%, push_2_sar 1.12%, push_0_shr 0.95%, push_i8_add 0.26%) plus the bare push_* short forms. 11.3% on the zoo census. These MOSTLY disappear under a register model -- JSC's Fits maps constants into the register index range (16..127 narrow) so `x | 0` needs no push, and V8 ships 12 Smi-immediate binary ops for the same reason -- but how much survives depends on register pressure and on whether the constant is loop-invariant. Reported separately so the verdict rests only on what is certain, while the upside is visible.

target_workloads.primary: the 15 zoo benchmarks that produced the 41.9e9-execution census (richards, deltablue, crypto, raytrace, navier-stokes, earley-boyer, regexp, splay, pdfjs, typescript, box2d, code-load, gbemu, mandreel, zlib)
target_workloads.reporting: per-benchmark breakdown is MANDATORY, not just a geomean. Rationale: the census corpus is synchronous, CPU-bound, old-style JS and fun is a runtime (opcode-design.md §4.7 limit four). A share that is carried by two benchmarks is a different fact from one that is uniform.
target_workloads.controls: none required -- there is no candidate arm

primary_metric: fraction of total suite cycles attributed to Tier 1, computed per benchmark and reported as a distribution (min / p10 / median / p90 / max across benchmarks), with Tier 2 reported alongside and instructions recorded in the same run

interpretation_bound.statement: The primary metric is an UPPER BOUND on the interpreter-side prize of option B, not an estimate of it.
interpretation_bound.why_upper: A measured handler's cycles include work that survives the model change (the slot read becomes an operand fetch folded into the consumer). A register machine removes the dispatch, the stack round trip and the refcount pair, not necessarily all of the handler body.
interpretation_bound.why_not_lower: It excludes second-order effects that could go either way -- I-cache footprint from fewer handlers, and the register machine's own added costs (liveness map for the exception path, opcode-design.md §9.3).

minimum_effect.continue: >= 20% of suite cycles in Tier 1 at the median benchmark -> K4's third precondition is met on the dispatch/operand-traffic axis; proceed to E1.5, and E2 becomes justifiable
minimum_effect.kill: median < 10% AND p90 < 20% -> the interpreter-side prize cannot support a 6721-line dispatch rewrite plus a compiler operand-allocation rewrite; option B drops to `later`
minimum_effect.ambiguous: anything else, including a split distribution (median < 10% but p90 >= 20%) -> do E1.5 first; a split means the prize is real on some workload shapes and absent on others, which is a scheduling question, not a kill
minimum_effect.why_not_set_near_the_measured_share: Tier 1 is ~43% of INSTRUCTIONS. The thresholds are about CYCLES, and the two are not interchangeable -- the registered instruction-phantom law is that removing instructions need not remove cycles (hand-written asm cut 16% of instructions for 0.0% of the time on the same dispatch skeletons). 10/20% therefore sit far below the instruction share on purpose: they ask whether the cycles are there at all, not whether they match the instruction count.
minimum_effect.basis: proposed -- owner approval required before the run, per roadmap 0.2 clause 5

maximum_regression.not_applicable: no candidate arm exists; nothing can regress

validity_requirements: Attribution MUST go through the dispatch table (see `method`), not through handler symbol names. Registered prior art for why symbol-level attribution needs a cross-check in this project: perf symbol merging has produced wrong attribution at least three times (2026-08-07 CodeLoad stage attribution, 2026-08-10 RayTrace, 2026-08-10/11 T6 counter diagnosis, which overturned three attributions and T7). IP -> handler must be resolved from the binary with nm -S ranges.
SPE share numbers are not admissible on their own (registered: 'SPE occupancy unreliable, trust only addr2line').

Handlers must be verified distinct in the measured binary: measured 216 distinct entries for 245 opcodes with zero unresolvable and no shared group straddling the measured/reference boundary (2026-08-27). Re-verify on any binary this is re-run against -- if LLVM ever merges two handlers across that boundary, the affected opcodes are reported as one bucket, never split by guess.
Measurement contract applies in full: pinned big core, host-heavy flock, insn and cycles in the same run, >= 8 samples, CV <= 5% or lengthen the workload.

The profiling build must NOT be used: -Dzjs_enable_opcode_profile=true adds noteDispatch to every dispatch and would be measuring the instrument. Use the shipping ReleaseFast binary; opcode identity comes from the dispatch table (see `method`), not from a counter and not from a symbol name.

Cold-shell handlers were checked and are NOT shared bodies: each coldStd(body) instantiation is comptime-distinct per opcode (nip, perm4 and rot3l resolve to three different coldStd__struct_*.h symbols). The earlier blanket caveat about the cold shell sharing function bodies was over-broad; the real sharing is the 15 groups listed in `method.resolution_measured`.

correctness_gates.binary_provenance: must record the frozen zjs binary sha256 and merge-base per BASE-G0, so the attribution can be re-run against the same artifact

size_cost_limit.basis: proposed -- one profiling run plus the table-location and nm -S mapping, which was already built and verified on 2026-08-27, so the remaining work is the perf run itself

sample_protocol: measurement contract (tools/compare/measurement_policy.json); >= 8 samples per benchmark, pinned big core, insn+cycles same run

verdicts.continue: median >= 20% -> record as K4 third-precondition evidence; E1.5 authorized; the parked E2 spike becomes ripe for re-deliberation with a sharper residual question
verdicts.ambiguous: median 10-20%, or any split distribution -> E1.5 first, then re-read this policy with the stack-round-trip component subtracted
verdicts.kill: median < 10% AND p90 < 20% -> option B goes to `later` on interpreter-benefit grounds. This kills option B's INTERPRETER argument only. It does not touch the FNABI three-address island (opcode-design.md 9.2), which needs slot-operand encoding regardless, nor does it revive the id-shortage argument (already dissolved in 9.1).
verdicts.distribution_clause: A median verdict may not be issued over a split distribution. If p90/median > 2, the per-benchmark table goes to owner review before any verdict is recorded -- a suite where integer loops show 25% and property-dense code shows 5% is a scheduling fact, not an average.

preregistration_note: Thresholds are fixed BEFORE the run precisely because both directions have strong post-hoc rationalisation pull: option B is architecturally attractive, and option A is the safe incumbent. Registered prior art for why this matters: PERF-T-SPIKE was written up as FAIL on 2026-08-26 and withdrawn on 2026-08-27 after the first-round workload was shown to hide the mechanism entirely.

method.status: verified end-to-end on the shipping binary, 2026-08-27, before the run
method.why_not_symbol_names: The hottest measured handlers are not named after their opcode. the 48-opcode slot-move family is about a third of dynamic instructions and get_loc* is its largest branch and its handler is emitted by the comptime factory opLoc(kind, idx_src), which returns an anonymous struct method; nm shows it as exec.tailcall_dispatch.opLoc__struct_108206.h. The symbols exist and no two share an address (no ICF merging), but the name does not say which opcode it serves. Attributing by symbol name would have silently mis-assigned exactly the set this policy exists to measure.
steps: 1. Locate the dispatch table in the binary: scan 8-byte-aligned windows for a run of 256 pointers into .text.zjs.op_handlers (vma 0x1070000, size 0x284a0 in the 2026-08-27 build).

2. SELF-CHECK, mandatory: cross-check the candidate table against the handlers that DO have op_<name> symbols. Measured: offset 0x3cb088 matches 72 of 73; the one difference is id 14 pointing at op_drop_fast rather than op_drop, which is the specialization the hot table is supposed to use. A candidate that does not clear this check is not the table.
3. nm -S gives (address, size) for every handler including the anonymous comptime instantiations.
4. Attribute each sampled IP to the handler whose [entry, entry+size) contains it.

resolution_measured.validity_note: No shared group straddles the measured-set / reference-set boundary: put_arg* and set_arg* are wholly inside the measured set, push_N and make_*_ref wholly inside the reference set. For this policy's question -- the measured set's share of cycles -- the 88% figure costs nothing.

method.binary_dependence: The table offset and section VMA are build-specific. Step 2's self-check is what makes the method safe to re-run against a different binary: re-locate, re-verify against the named handlers, and only then attribute.
